subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Dan Cong: Phoenix Oolongs
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Dan Cong: Phoenix Oolongs.

hook.text: Phoenix Mountain in Guangdong, China, grows oolongs that naturally mimic the aroma of orchid, honey, and fruit.

buildup.text: Dan Cong means 'single bush.' Each tree produces tea with a distinct aroma—no two trees taste the same.

discovery.text: Some trees are centuries old. The oldest Dan Cong trees produce tiny amounts that sell for extraordinary prices.

twist.text: These teas mimic flavors like grapefruit, ginger flower, and almond—without any added ingredients.

climax.text: Dan Cong production is risky. One mistake in charcoal roasting can ruin a batch worth thousands of dollars.

punchline.text: One bush, one aroma, unrepeatable. Nature's originals.

quiz.question: What does 'Dan Cong' mean?
options: Single bush—each tree has its own unique character

details.summary: Dan Cong oolongs from Phoenix Mountain in Guangdong are prized for mimicking specific natural fragrances like honey orchid, almond, and ginger flower. Each tree produces a distinct flavor profile, and leaves from individual trees can sell for extraordinary prices.
details.whyItMatters: Dan Cong teas demonstrate how a single tea tree's genetics and microclimate can produce irreplaceable flavors, making individual trees as valued as vineyards.
takeaways: Each Dan Cong tree has a unique flavor profile
Named varieties mimic natural fragrances like honey orchid
Phoenix Mountain in Guangdong is the sole origin

faq.question: What does Dan Cong mean in Chinese?
faq.answer: Dan Cong literally means single bush, referring to the tradition of harvesting and processing leaves from individual trees separately. This preserves each tree's unique character. Some ancient Dan Cong trees are hundreds of years old and produce only a few kilograms of tea per year.

faq.question: What is the most famous Dan Cong variety?
faq.answer: Mi Lan Xiang, or Honey Orchid fragrance, is the most popular and widely available. It has a sweet, lychee-like aroma with a honeyed finish. Ya Shi Xiang (duck shit fragrance, despite the name) is another prized variety known for its intense floral and mineral character.
